content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1: turn on IVR callback for payments 18:00–20:00. It costs nothing and keeps the 16:00–20:00 window at a predicted 83.3% against the 80% target.","why":"General calls have run about 30% over forecast all day (2,600 vs 2,003.8 so far). The rise is spread evenly across every call reason, with no customer-facing incident or campaign behind it, so there is no single cause to fix. Even so, the overall window is predicted to stay above target: 82.9% with no action and 83.3% with P1. P1 is the cheapest compliant plan that reaches 80%. It also trims predicted abandons from 4.8% to 4.5% and lifts payments to 87.9%.","trade_offs":["General queue stays below target: P1 predicts general at 78.2%, slightly worse than 78.9% with no action. The overall 83.3% is propped up by payments at 87.9%.","P2 (₹2,424) is the targeted fix for the surge. It adds overtime for 8 general agents plus balance-enquiry chat deflection and lifts general to 92.1% and overall to 91.5%, with abandons at 2.2%.","P4 (₹2,280) is cheaper than P2 and reaches 92.9% overall (general 91.3%, abandons 1.8%), though it relies more on deflection.","P3 (₹3,660) is the strongest at 93.8% overall and 1.5% abandons, at the highest cost."],"watch":"The overall margin is thin at 3.3 points, and general is already predicted to miss 80%. If general calls keep rising beyond the current 14–39% over forecast, or overall service level trends toward 80% before 18:00, switch to P4 or P2 to add general capacity."}
